A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same C2BM research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, causal-graph recovery, intervention, debiasing, and fairness experiments, with additional analyses in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds results including CUBC, reduced concept bottlenecks, SCBM comparisons, and causal-discovery ablations.

M1.justification: The architecture, adaptive linear structural equations, and GES plus retrieval-augmented LLM pipeline remain. The reported training recipe changes: v1 uses loss weight 0.5 and training intervention probability 0.8; v2 specifies concept-loss weight 0.8 and intervention probability 0.25. These are limited training changes, not a redesigned model.

E1.justification: v2 adds CUBC, a bird-image task with constructed concepts and a survival target, while retaining the earlier benchmark collection. cMNIST changes from two to three colors and from randomized test colors to reversed color-parity association. Asia* and Alarm* retain existing data and tasks with reduced concept bottlenecks.

E2.justification: v2 adds SCBM to accuracy, intervention, and fairness comparisons. The original joint-output opaque baseline is retained as OpaqNNM in Table 6, while a task-only OpaqNN enters the main comparison; opaque curves disappear from the intervention figures. New Table 8 evaluates PC, FGES, their LLM/RAG refinements, and direct LLM-based graph recovery.

E3.justification: Fixed learning rates and widths in v1 give way to validation-based hyperparameter searches in v2, alongside revised loss weighting and training intervention frequency. v2 adds reduced-bottleneck protocols and separates task accuracy from joint label accuracy. Intervention evaluation changes from grouped graph levels and cumulative relative improvement to random concepts within levels, concept counts, and absolute accuracy.

E4.justification: v2 adds a substantial causal-discovery method ablation across five Bayesian networks, reduced-concept expressivity tests, and a worked interpretability case in Appendix D.2. Intervention and debiasing analyses are revised. The earlier true-versus-learned graph, single-concept intervention, LLM-size, and RAG analyses remain under new numbering.

E5.justification: Matched accuracy tables change uncertainty reporting from one to two sample-mean sigma while retaining five seeds. v2 Table 1 also marks significant improvements in bold without specifying a significance test. No increase in experimental run counts is documented.

E6.justification: Joint label results are updated: for example, C2BM's Hailfinder accuracy is 67.25% in v1 Table 1 and 71.85% in v2 Table 6. Task accuracy, intervention curves, and true-versus-learned graph results are revised or expanded, with new CUBC, reduced-bottleneck, SCBM, and discovery results. Changed settings limit direct performance comparison. Table 2 and the pre-existing fairness rows remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem D.1, claiming universal approximation regardless of the causal graph, with a proof covering root, single-parent, multiple-parent, and recursive cases. v1 contains no corresponding theorem or proof. Its standalone causal-probabilistic graphical-model definition and Markov-property equation in Appendix A.2 are omitted.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a causal concept bottleneck and automated construction pipeline, maintaining predictive accuracy while improving causal reliability, interventions, debiasing, and fairness. Expanded evidence does not materially redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes approximating outcomes from identifying true structural functions in Remark 4.5. It adds explanations contrasting causal propagation with SCBM's associative propagation, a weighted prediction example, and scientific hypothesis-screening applications. Existing limitations concerning knowledge quality, scalability, and encoder distribution shifts remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies concept-filter thresholds, GES library and scoring details, ten-query aggregation, synthetic embedding dimensions, SCBM configuration, GPU models, and an explicit code-repository link. CUBC construction rules are documented. Conversely, v1's explicit intervention-test noise setting and detailed standalone baseline descriptions are no longer provided.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantive positioning against SCBM, newer concept-model citations, and references supporting the expanded causal-discovery discussion. Some opacity and software references disappear. The principal positioning relative to conventional CBMs, DiConStruct, and neural causal models remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, preliminaries, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Related work moves before the method, instantiation and training receive separate treatment, and the appendices are reorganized around pipeline components with a contents page. These changes substantially alter the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The main text switches from two columns to one, with extensive figure and table rearrangement. v2 adds nonlinear-function, worked-prediction, and fairness diagrams. Intervention plots use new axes and comparison panels, while accuracy and discovery tables gain substantial structural changes.

improvement.justification: Separate task-accuracy reporting, SCBM comparisons, and the expanded graph-discovery ablation better test the central claims, while added implementation details improve reproducibility. These gains are tempered by omitted test-noise documentation and inconsistent intervention reporting: Appendix G.7 still describes cumulative relative improvement although Figure 12 plots accuracy. The net improvement is useful but qualified.
